trust_decision.summary: A soft-lock contender decides that the file now at the lock path is the same marker it judged stale (dead owner, aged malformed record, expired lifetime/lease), identified only by (mtime, inode), and then renames/unlinks it; a reused inode number or a recreate in the rename window lets it remove a live holder's marker.

landing_point.why: Summary names the SoftFileLock stale-lock break; SoftFileLock._try_break_stale_lock reads (mtime, ino) and calls break_lock_file (src/filelock/_util.py:86).

SoftFileLock.acquire() malformed-marker self-heal and SoftFileLease lease-expiry timer (src/filelock/_lease.py:267)
SoftFileLock.acquire() rollback when writing the record fails or is interrupted

O3_reason_to_dismiss: UnixFileLock is the flock-based FileLock, not a soft lock, and the ENOSYS fallback is a rare-filesystem corner; the lifetime break lives in the base class and is a separate 'lifetime' feature, so a solver fixing SoftFileLock's stale check can argue both are outside the report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A genuinely dead holder's marker, an aged malformed/empty marker, and a lifetime- or lease-expired marker must still be reclaimed automatically, and break_lock()/force_break() must still remove any marker; a fix that never breaks (or always waits for timeout) breaks stale-lock recovery.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SoftFileLock.release fallback: when the unlink while open fails, the marker is unlinked by (dev, ino) identity after the fd is closed, so the inode is no longer pinned and a successor's marker could carry the same number; the fix did not change this call.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only reached when unlink-while-open fails (SMB-style shares); the in-code comment argues the still-present marker keeps the inode allocated, and it needs a lifetime-expired hold broken by a peer.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as landing point, release path (~100 lines below)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: StrictSoftFileLock._occupant_unchanged_for keys an occupant on (mtime, ino, size) without ctime, the same identity key the fix had to extend; a variant that evicts the occupant after the grace would be a reused-inode sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Its comment says it copies SoftFileLock's marker rule, so a maintainer could plausibly have made it break rather than raise.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same 'unlink by name after close' idiom already exists for the OS-lock backend; a soft-backend copy is natural.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The helper already compares lstat identities for the link/replace protocol; reusing it for stale eviction is a one-line change.
